3. Material 

Components Material 

Arms, locking plate and Stainless steel 

catch 
Rivets and guide-cum- Stainless steel 

locking pin 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 Arms shall be finished smooth and free from burrs, pits, cracks, etc. 

4.2 Jaws shall open and close with even movement. 

4.3 The pins In the case of Prince's forceps shall register in holes accurately without sticking or locking. 
When the arms are pressed, the pin nearer the tip shall register first and on pressing the arms further the 
other pins shall register. 

4.4 The registration of the jaws shall correspond with the registration of guide-cum-locking pin in the 
guide hole. 

4.5 The locking device shall move smoothly and once locked shall not unlock by slipping. 

4.6 Pins and serrations shall be clean and bright. 

4.7 Pins shall be semi-sharp. 

4.8 Forceps shall be passivated and polished bright. 

5. Heat Treatment — The Instrument shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 430 to 490 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Test for Engagement of Serrations — As in Section I of IS : 3642-l966t. With serrations fully engaged 
the tips shall not gape. 

6.2 When the Prince's forceps is fully closed and locked the tips shall not gape. 

6.3 Apply load at the end of the finger grooves proximal to the tip to make the tips just touch. The 
load required shall be 225 ± 20 gf for Prince's forceps and 200 ± 20 gf for Worth's forceps. 

6.4 The arms of the forceps after maximum closure by manual compression shall not take a permanent set 
and the tips sJmJI continue to engage and disengage accurately and properly. 

'^ ' -r.'-- '^ .t^^ ' ^f - v- ■ - 

♦Schedirtesfbr wrought steels for general engineering purposes. 
fGeneral requirements for surgical instruments. 



IS : 5367 - 1969 

6.5 Grip a piece of vulcanized rubber 6 mm thick between the tips of the Worth's forceps. Apply 
maximum pressure with thumb and forefingers to close the tips. Release the grip. The forceps shall not 
show any sign of damage and the jaws shall continue to engage and disengage accurately. 

6.6 Grip the joint end firmly in a vice. Apply a force at the tip to deflect it in a plane at right angles to 
the plane of the arm by 20 mm. Release the force. No permanent set shall be observed. Repeat the test 
on the other arm. 

6.7 Corrosion Resistance — Scrub the sample with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and then dip in 
95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the sample. Immerse in copper sulphate solution at room temperature for 
6 minutes and wash off with fresh water or wee cotton wool. Make up the solution as follows; 

Copper sulphate ( CuSO^.SHgO ) 4*0 g 

Sulphuric acid ( H2SO4 ) (spgr h84) iO-Og 

Water ( HgO ) 90-0 mi 

No red stains or spots on the sample shall be allowed but dulling of the polished surface may be 
permitted* 

7. Marking — Mark with the following; 

a) Manufacturer's name or initials or recognized trade-mark, and 

b) The words * stainless steel '. 

7.1 iSi Certification Mark — Details available from Indian Standards institution, New Delhi I. 

8. Packing — The forceps shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or packed in polyethylene bag, avoid- 
ing contact with one another.
